case_results.review: The top five are inexpensive Ninja, combat-damage, card-flow, and interaction upgrades. Wash Out is an unprotected flex cut; evasive enablers, reveal-value cards, typal density, and the no-fast-mana constraint remain intact.
The portfolio supplies card flow, protection, and an on-type Elf. Overwhelming Stampede is preserved; the Wood Elves swap is like-for-like on Elf density and all measured floors remain intact.
Affordable token draw, proliferate utility, a recursive Insect answer, recursion, and removal all fit the graveyard-sacrifice plan. Declared outlets and toolbox creatures are protected.
Tutorable Aura interaction leads, two additional Auras preserve the ladder, and two inexpensive ramp choices address the measured mana gap without converting the deck to Equipment Voltron.

Every addition is an instant or sorcery with interaction, protection, card flow, or tempo value. Narrow colorless-mana false positives and the unsafe Bident cut are absent; spell density is preserved.

The engine returns only two high-evidence donation cards and abstains from generic control filler. Political defenses and donation packages survive; the cuts remove an alternate-win diversion and an off-plan body.
The additions cover velocity, protection/evasion, Goblin density, acceleration, and repeatable token draw. Pyrokinesis and compact combo pieces are protected, and no unsafe cut is offered.

Three of five cards are efficient blink or blink-interaction spells, with card flow and protection filling measured needs. Conditional mana creatures and weak fixing claims are excluded, Chromatic Lantern is preserved, and the engine abstains from cuts.

The full top five costs less than two dollars in current catalog prices and directly supplies sacrifice, recursion, Zombie density, and card velocity. Unsupported discard and attack-trigger suggestions are gone.

Five efficient stack-interaction cards protect budget spell-chain lines. Unrelated counter domains, unsafe Urabrask cuts, unpriced fast mana, and premium cards above the soft budget proxy no longer enter the selected portfolio.

Curated competitive evidence produces efficient interaction, acceleration, library access, an asymmetric reset, and protection. Protected stack interaction remains; Machine God's Effigy is the only measured flex cut.

The output is entirely tournament-speed interaction, fast mana, or competitive card advantage, with no casual Ninja filler and zero top-five overlap with budget Yuriko. Nanogene Conversion is protected as a compact board-copy closer.
One-mana interaction, a compact tutor, and efficient red/blue stack answers match the tournament plan. Untap text is no longer called extra combat, and Gogo is protected as a combat-copy enabler.

Preserve mode returns one on-plan donation card and abstains from all cuts and generic optimization. Gilded Drake and other curated power outliers are excluded from the intentionally janky experience.

The severe land warning remains explicit while the declared low-land premise suppresses blind repair. All additions are affordable and on the Insect, token, sacrifice, or graveyard plan; the commander duplicate and unrelated counter card are gone.
Extreme repetition is detected, analysis remains stable, and additions, cuts, and swaps are paused rather than repairing the joke deck.
The 98-card state and missing commander are preserved. Analysis is blocked with both exact reasons and no recommendations are generated.
The 23-card main deck, 24 submitted cards, and zero lands are preserved. Severe incompleteness blocks analysis without fabricating a complete deck.
